function.description: Retrieves a list of API tokens associated with the user's account. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: api_token_api_APITokenApi_post_api_token
function.description: Create a new API token for authenticating against the API endpoints. The token ensures secure access to the provided services. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

permissions.description: The level of access granted by the token.

expiration_date.description: The expiration date of the token in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If not provided, the token will expire in 1 year by default.

message.content:
I’m happy to help!  
Just so I understand exactly what you’re trying to accomplish, could you let me know:

* **Do you already have a token stored somewhere** and simply want to look up its details (e.g., who owns it, when it expires, its permission level)?  
* **Or are you hoping to *retrieve the literal token string* that was issued earlier**, so you can paste it into another service now?  

A quick heads‑up: most systems don’t allow you to pull back the original token text once it’s been created—this protects the key from accidental exposure. What you can normally do instead is:

| Action | Typical Endpoint |
|--------|------------------|
| View token metadata (ID, owner, expiry, permissions) | `GET /api/tokens/{userId}` (`api_token_api_APITokenApi_get_api_tokens`) |
| Generate a brand‑new token (and receive the plain text right away) | `POST /api/token` (`api_token_api_APITokenApi_post_api_token`) |

Let me know which route fits your needs—or if there’s something else entirely—and I’ll walk through the exact steps (or even make the API calls on your behalf!).
